source.title: Data-optimal scaling of paired antibody language models
source.authors: Mahdi Shafiei Neyestanak; Sarah M. Burbach; Karenna Ng; P. Gangavarapu; Jonathan Hurtado; J. Magura; N. Ismail; Daniel Muema; T. Ndung'u; A. Ward; Bryan S. Briney

record.file_problem: Full preprint text is present. Figure and supplementary-table captions are included, but their plotted/tabulated values are not rendered in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures held-out loss across model and data scales in paired antibody language models and develops a data-optimal scaling relation. Its results refine the generalization of compute-focused scaling to a data-limited setting.
record.gate_note: The study reports MLM-loss measurements for 15 model–data configurations and reports a fitted power law for optimal data size versus model size. Downstream classification results also bear on scale-related predictability. Per-residue CDRH3 results and detailed confusion-matrix results are not included as rows because they do not measure the versions’ stated scaling behavior. Cited scaling-law results from other studies are not treated as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study trains 15 ESM-2-style masked LMs on paired antibody sequences (8M–650M parameters × 0.4M/0.8M/1.6M sequences). It measures held-out MLM loss and downstream classification and fits a power law for optimal data versus model size. This is a new modality (V5) with downstream-scaling results (V6). It is not text LM pretraining, so V1–V4 are not tested as stated. Compute is unconstrained: 500k steps on every dataset, so many epochs, with checkpoints chosen at the onset of overfitting.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that paired AbLMs are data-limited and that optimal data scales as a power law of model size. A 650M AbLM would need ~5.5M paired sequences (after 90% clustering), about twice what OAS holds. Downstream tasks favour 350M, above the ~152M loss-optimum, and 650M degrades, so model size and data must be scaled jointly.
record.recipe_differences: Uses paired antibody sequences and masked-language-model evaluation; constructs FixedData profiles by fitting quadratic loss curves over log parameter count and fits a power law to their minima. It does not reproduce the original compute-optimal language-model experiments or their loss-fitting procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimal model size varies with training-data scale. Loss-based estimates and downstream-task performance differ; the authors note that fixed-data loss profiles may underestimate downstream-optimal model size. The loss-fit procedure retains points near each minimum and excludes distant outliers.

fits_no_version.finding: With training data fixed and compute unconstrained (multi-epoch, early-stopped), loss versus model size is U-shaped. The loss-minimising model size grows with data, giving optimal data ∝ N^0.84.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In data-limited regimes with unconstrained compute, the loss-optimal model size for a fixed dataset grows as a power of dataset size.

record.problems: Only five model sizes and three training-data scales were tested. The power-law extrapolation is based on minima from three data-scale profiles; loss-profile outliers far from minima were excluded. Exact plotted loss and many downstream metric values are unavailable in the supplied text. The study does not test compute-optimal allocation or independent variation of tokens and compute.
record.rows_left_out: Per-residue CDRH3 loss outcomes by region and mutation status (Figure 3 and Table S3) were omitted because they are regional prediction metrics rather than the held-out pretraining-loss scaling measure in V1. The confusion matrix was omitted because it does not test scale predictability. The study’s detailed subgroup analyses beyond the stated mutation-count result were not separately extracted.

untested.parts: Text-LM pretraining loss; no power-law fit of loss to N, D or C anywhere.
No extrapolation of loss to larger runs. The 650M data estimate is not checked against a trained run.
No fixed-compute allocation. Compute is unconstrained and data is held fixed.
Shape is not varied at a fixed parameter count.
No power law of loss itself in the antibody domain. Image/video, fine-tuning and transfer scaling are not tested. The repeated-data regime is not analysed as such.
No variation of parameter counting, schedule, outlier exclusion or fitting method, and no comparison of exponents.

missing.what: Loss-optimal model size for Dataset-F (~152M) versus downstream-optimal size (350M). The loss optimum underestimates the downstream optimum.
missing.locator: Discussion, paragraph on downstream tasks; Results after Figure 4

missing.what: Binary specificity accuracy rises with data scale for all model sizes except 8M (35M–650M not recorded as a row).
FixedData optimal model size increases with data scale; the three minima themselves are not recorded as values.

record.verdict_notes: Domain is antibody sequences, so the results are routed to V5 rather than V1. Tranche changed from T5 to T3. Rows R1–R15 are one configuration each with figure-only values and would be better collapsed. The power-law fit has two parameters fitted to three points, so the high R² is weak evidence. Training ran 500k steps × batch 128 on 0.4–1.6M sequences, i.e. many epochs (heavily repeated data).

versions.untested_parts: The study measures MLM loss across five model sizes and three data sizes, but does not fit a power law for loss against parameters, tokens, or compute; does not vary training tokens independently of sequence count; and does not test the regime where data and compute are not bottlenecks or a several-orders-of-magnitude range.
The study extrapolates optimal data requirements from fitted FixedData minima, not losses of larger runs from loss fits on small runs.
The study considers data-optimal model size with training data held fixed, not a fixed compute budget or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
Architecture details are not varied at a fixed parameter count.
The study tests paired antibody sequence pretraining, not image or video models, repeated-data training, fine-tuning scaling laws, or transfer scaling laws.

The study reports downstream classification outcomes across scale but does not fit a predictive relationship from pretraining loss to downstream performance or evaluate broad downstream task families.

The study shows dependence on data scale and evaluation objective and describes its fitting procedure, but does not systematically vary parameter-count conventions, training schedules, datasets, or fitting methods, nor compare exponents against the original studies.

rows.subject: FixedData minima across AbLM sizes and training datasets
rows.operation_detail: Fit a power-law regression to optimal model-size minima from FixedData profiles to estimate optimal training-data size.
rows.measure: Relationship between optimal training-data size and model size
rows.value: Data size = 0.232 × (Model Size)^0.8369; R² = 0.9997; estimated ~5.5M paired sequences for a 650M-parameter AbLM
rows.locator: Methods, FixedData Evaluation; Results, Figure 2b; Discussion
rows.note: This is a fitted relation for optimal data requirements, not a power-law fit to held-out loss. FixedData profiles fit a quadratic function of log-transformed parameter count; points far from each minimum were excluded.
rows.check: Power law of optimal data versus model size, fitted to only three FixedData minima. It is not a loss power law and not at fixed compute. V7 link removed: fit sensitivity was not examined.

rows.subject: 8M AbLMs (aggregate across Dataset-F, Dataset-H, and Dataset-Q)
rows.operation_detail: Compared binary CoV-specific versus healthy-donor classification accuracy across pretraining data scales.
rows.value: Models performed equivalently regardless of pretraining data scale.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error across 5-fold CV replicates is described for the figure; values not stated in text.
rows.note: Aggregate result for the 8M models as reported by the authors.

rows.subject: 350M-F and 350M-H AbLMs
rows.operation_detail: Compared binary CoV-specific versus healthy-donor classification accuracy across pretraining data scales.
rows.value: 350M-F significantly outperformed 350M-H; numeric accuracies not stated in text.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error across 5-fold CV replicates is described for the figure; significance value not stated.
rows.note: The authors report the largest performance separation at 350M parameters.

rows.subject: 650M AbLMs
rows.operation_detail: Compared binary antibody specificity classification performance with the 350M models.
rows.value: No further improvement was observed at 650M; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.note: The authors report similar trends across other classification metrics.

rows.subject: 350M-F AbLM
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated on three-way CoV-specific, influenza-specific, and healthy-donor antibody classification.
rows.baseline: other tested model sizes and data scales
rows.value: Performed best across the classification metrics; numeric values not stated in text.
rows.note: The authors state that 350M-F consistently outperformed other models across model sizes and data scales on the classification tasks.
rows.check: This is a best-model ranking, not a scaling trend. It is consistent with gains up to 350M with more data.

rows.subject: AbLMs across tested sizes and data scales
rows.operation_detail: Compared native and randomly shuffled heavy/light chain pairs using 5-fold cross-validation.
rows.value: Even the smallest models exceeded random guessing; improvement over that baseline was not observed until 350M parameters.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error across 5-fold CV replicates is described for the figure; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.note: Aggregate statement across the tested model sizes.

rows.subject: 650M AbLMs
rows.operation_detail: Compared chain-pair classification performance with the 350M models.
rows.value: 650M models consistently performed worse than 350M models; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error across 5-fold CV replicates is described for the figure; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.note: The paper reports the same general reduction for the 650M models on downstream tasks.
rows.check: The 650M models sit beyond the data-optimal size under fixed data, so this is a reversal in model-size scaling without matched data.

rows.subject: 350M AbLM classifiers
rows.operation_detail: Compared native and shuffled pair predictions across pretraining data scales and examined mutation-count subgroups.
rows.measure: Correct predictions by class and classification accuracy
rows.baseline: 350M classifiers at lower pretraining data scales; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.value: With increasing data scale, gains were driven by more correct native-pair classifications; shuffled-pair classification remained largely unchanged. Gains were concentrated on native pairs with low and similar mutation counts (1–7 mutations) in both chains.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error of prediction counts across 5-fold CV is described for Figure 5b; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.note: The authors attribute this outcome to models learning a chain-specific mutation-count heuristic.
rows.check: Mostly a mechanism breakdown of what drives the gains. V7 link removed: no fitting-choice dependence.

relationships.condition: Paired-antibody MLM pretraining, 8M–650M parameters, 0.4–1.6M sequences, multi-epoch
relationships.reason: The optimal data size follows a power law in model size (exponent 0.837, R²=0.9997), but the fit uses only three FixedData minima and is not a loss power law (R16).
relationships.display_finding: Optimal data size scaled with model size with exponent 0.837 and R² of 0.9997, based on three fixed-data minima.

relationships.condition: Models at or near 350M parameters, scaling pretraining data from Q to F
relationships.reason: 350M-F significantly beats 350M-H and is the best model overall; data-driven gains in native-pair classification (R18, R20, R23).
relationships.display_finding: 350M-F significantly outperformed 350M-H and achieved the best overall native-pair classification performance.

relationships.condition: Very small models, and model size scaled beyond the data-optimal size under fixed data
relationships.reason: 8M gains nothing from more data (R17). Pair-task gains appear only at 350M (R21). 650M shows no gain on specificity (R19) and is worse on pairing (R22). The text also says loss-optimal size (~152M) underestimates the downstream-optimal size.
relationships.display_finding: The 8M model gained nothing from more data, pairing gains appeared only at 350M, and 650M added no specificity gain while worsening pairing; the loss-optimal size of about 152M underestimated the downstream optimum.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Data-limited paired-antibody pretraining at the tested model and data scales
reader_labels.reason: The study measures held-out loss across scales but fits a quadratic loss profile with an interior optimum rather than demonstrating a power law for loss; the tested setting is explicitly data-limited (R1–R16).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The authors report an AbLM-specific power-law fit relating optimal training-data size to model size and extrapolate it to a 650M-parameter model (R16).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Downstream specificity and chain-pair classification tasks
reader_labels.reason: Scale-related performance is not uniformly increasing: 8M specificity classifiers did not benefit from added data, 650M models did not improve on 350M for specificity and were worse for pair classification, while larger/data-rich configurations showed gains (R17–R23).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: FixedData MLM-loss fits and downstream classification in paired AbLMs
reader_labels.reason: Optimal model size changes with data scale, the loss profile is fitted quadratically near its minimum with distant points excluded, and downstream-optimal sizes differ from the loss-based estimate (R1–R16, R18–R23).
